description: PAM is a Python library for creating and modifying synthetic populations and their activity sequences. The JOSS article gives transport and energy demand examples, including travel to a new station and electric-vehicle uptake. The own Zenodo software archive identifies the package and MIT licence, so the archived code is free under those terms. Inputs can include travel diaries, existing synthetic agents, locations and activity rules. Outputs are scenario populations or sequences for downstream transport simulations, including MATSim-compatible formats. Geographic and temporal coverage depend on the user population and activity schedule. Infrastructure modellers could use PAM to generate travel demand for road or transit capacity testing. A caveat is that synthetic activities must be calibrated to local surveys; plausible daily patterns do not prove future behaviour. The paper-linked GitHub repository returns 404, so present maintenance and installation from that address remain unverified. No directly related catalogue record was confirmed. The archive files were not downloaded.
